IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r6.claim: Other prophetic miracles occurred at particular times, circumstances, and audiences, and were transmitted at differing levels; the Quran is a general miracle for all generations.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r7.claim: The Quran repeatedly challenged the Arabs to produce a comparable surah or ten surahs; its explicit record that they would fail was fulfilled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r7.anchor: تتحدى العرب بأن يأتوا بسورة مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r8.claim: History confirms the challengers' inability: despite a long period in disbelief, they produced no matching surah and instead turned to armed resistance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p101#2/r8.anchor: فالتحدي متواتر وعجز المتحدين أيضا متواتر بشهادة التاريخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives poetic and proverbial examples of compact idiomatic expressions relevant to Quranic interpretation, says comparable usage is plentiful, and allows that some may involve an omitted genitive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.anchor: وفي هذه الأمثلة كفاية فيما نحوناه إذ النظير لذلك كثير موجود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r1.speaker: إياس بن معاوية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r1.claim: Ibn Muʿāwiya compares understanding tafsir to receiving a letter at night: without a lamp its recipients are distressed, but light lets them understand it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r1.anchor: وقال إياس بن معاوية مثل من يقرأ القرآن ومن يعلم تفسيره أو لا يعلم مثل قوم جاءهم كتاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r2.speaker: قوم يميلون إلى العربية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r2.claim: Arabic-oriented scholars, the majority of early commentators, treat tafsir and taʾwīl as synonymous.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r2.anchor: فذهب قوم يميلون إلى العربية إلى أنهما بمعنى وهذا قول جمهور المفسرين المتقدمين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r3.speaker: قوم يميلون إلى الفقه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r3.claim: Fiqh-oriented scholars distinguish them: tafsir brings a matter from obscurity to clarity, while taʾwīl redirects speech from its apparent sense with evidence; taʾwīl derives from a thing becoming something.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r3.anchor: وذهب قوم يميلون إلى الفقه إلى اختلافهما فقالوا التفسير إخراج الشيء من مقام الخفاء إلى مقام التجلى والتأويل نقل الكلام عن وضعه فيما يحتاج فى إثباته إلى دليل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports through ʿIkrima that the whole Quran descended on Laylat al-Qadr from the Preserved Tablet to the House of Might, then came down over twenty years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r4.anchor: روى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ فى ليلة القدر إلى بيت العزة ثم انزل بعد ذلك فى عشرين سنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r5.speaker: الشعبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the Quran's revelation was apportioned and twenty years passed between its beginning and end.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it was reported that eighteen years passed between the Quran's beginning and end, with eight years of revelation in Mecca.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن ذكر لنا أنه كان بين أوله وآخره ثماني عشرة سنة انزل عليه بمكة ثمانى سنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r7.speaker: عائشة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r7.claim: The established report from ʿĀʾisha, transmitted by ʿUrwa and supported by Qatāda and Abū Ṣāliḥ, identifies Iqraʾ as the first revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r7.anchor: رواه عروة عن عائشة وبه قال قتادة وأبوا صالح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r8.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r8.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports that al-Muddaththir was the first revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r8.anchor: وروي عن جابر به عبد الله أن أول ما نزل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r9.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī reconciles the reports: Iqraʾ came first, then after the Prophet returned and covered himself, al-Muddaththir was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r9.anchor: والصحيح أنه لما نزل عليه ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾ رجع فتدثر فنزل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r10.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r10.claim: In the Ṣaḥīḥayn report about the pause in revelation, the Prophet sees the angel between heaven and earth, returns terrified asking to be covered, and then receives al-Muddaththir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r10.anchor: ما أخرج فى الصحيحين من حديث جابر قال سمعت النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يحدث عن فترة الوحى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r11.claim: The phrase juthittu means I was frightened, as in majʾūth or majthūth; some transmitters corrupted it to jabuntu, from cowardice, but the former is correct.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r11.anchor: ومعنى جثتت فرقت يقال رجل مجؤوث ومجثوث وقد صحفه بعض الرواة فقال جبنت من الجبن والصحيح الأول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r12.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r12.claim: A report from al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima says the basmala was the first revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p4/r12.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعكرمة أن أول ما نزل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.claim: Usayd ibn Hudayr recited al-Baqara at night; his horse repeatedly startled as he recited and quieted when he stopped, so he left to protect his nearby son Yahya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.anchor: عن أسيد بن الحضير قال: بينما هو يقرأ من الليل سورة البقرة، وفرسه مربوطة عنده، إذ جالت الفرس، فسكت فسكنت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.claim: Usayd saw a canopy-like cloud filled with lamps rise away; the Prophet told him angels had drawn near to his recitation and would have become visible had he continued.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.anchor: فرفعت رأسي إلى السماء فإذا مثل الظلة، فيها أمثال المصابيح، فخرجت حتى لا أراها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir notes Bukhari cites the report without a connected chain and criticizes its first route: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi was a junior Successor who did not meet Usayd, and the attribution is unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.anchor: هكذا أورد البخاري هذا الحديث معلقا، وفيه انقطاع في الرواية الأولى، فإن محمد بن إبراهيم بن الحارث التيمي المدني تابعي صغير لم يدرك أسيدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir says he found no connected route through al-Layth except the one Ibn ʿAsakir's al-Atraf attributes to Yahya ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Bukayr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.anchor: ولم أره بسند متصل عن الليث بذلك، إلا ما ذكره الحافظ أبو القاسم بن عساكر في الأطراف أن يحيى بن عبد الله بن بكير رواه عن الليث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayd transmits the account through al-Layth and Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from Usayd, then adds a corroborating route through ʿAbd Allah ibn Khabbab, Abu Saʿid, and Usayd.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.anchor: فقال: حدثنا عبد الله بن صالح ويحيى بن بكير، عن الليث، عن يزيد بن عبد الله بن أسامة بن الهاد، عن محمد بن إبراهيم بن الحارث التيمي، عن أسيد بن حضير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.claim: Al-Nasa'i transmits a route through ʿAbd Allah ibn Khabbab from Abu Saʿid from Usayd; Yahya ibn Bukayr likewise combines the two routes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.anchor: عن يزيد بن عبد الله، وهو ابن الهاد، عن عبد الله بن خباب، عن أبي سعيد، عن أسيد، به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.claim: In the al-Manaqib version, the wording does not explicitly say the report is from Usayd, though Ibn Kathir says that is its apparent meaning; he leaves the matter to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.anchor: ولم يقل: عن أسيد، ولكن ظاهره أنه عنه، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r1.claim: Al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib says he learned “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High” before the Prophet arrived; the report is agreed upon and belongs to the Hijra narrative.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r1.anchor: سمع البراء بن عازب يقول: تعلمت {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} قبل أن يقدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir takes the report as evidence that al-Aʿla was revealed in Mecca before the Hijra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r2.anchor: والمراد منه أن {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} مكية نزلت قبل الهجرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud identified twenty paired surahs the Prophet recited two at a time in each rakʿa; in his ordering, they began the Mufassal and ended with al-Dukhan and ʿAmma yatasa'alun.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r3.anchor: قال عبد الله: لقد علمت النظائر التي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Ibn Masʿud's reported arrangement strange and contrary to ʿUthman's codex: the Mufassal there runs from al-Hujurat to the end, excluding al-Dukhan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r4.anchor: وهذا التأليف الذي عن ابن مسعود غريب مخالف لتأليف عثمان، رضي الله عنه، فإن المفصل في مصحف عثمان، رضي الله عنه، من سورة الحجرات إلى آخره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r5.speaker: أوس بن حذيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r5.claim: Aws ibn Hudhayfa reports that the Prophet once stayed in after ʿIsha to finish a Qur'anic portion; the Companions divided recitation into groups of three, five, seven, nine, eleven, and thirteen surahs, then the Mufassal from Qaf to the end. Ibn Kathir grades the chain hasan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p49/r5.anchor: عن جده أوس بن حذيفة قال: كنت في الوفد الذين أتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر حديثا فيه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يسمر معهم بعد العشاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Gabriel began by reciting on one letter, while the Prophet kept asking for more until he was granted seven; the report is also transmitted by Bukhari, Muslim, and Ibn Jarir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r1.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r2.speaker: الزهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r2.claim: Al-Zuhri says the seven modes concern the same matter and do not differ over what is lawful or forbidden.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r2.anchor: ثم قال الزهري: بلغني أن تلك السبعة الأحرف إنما هي في الأمر الذي يكون واحدا لا تختلف في حلال ولا في حرام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports that Gabriel and Mika'il granted seven modes after two people recited a verse differently; the Prophet confirmed both, and each mode is sufficient and complete.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p35#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال: ما حاك في صدري شيء منذ أسلمت، إلا أنني قرأت آية وقرأها آخر غير قراءتي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb took a man whose recitation the Prophet approved to the Prophet, who approved Ubayy's different recitation too, prayed to remove his doubt, and explained that angels granted seven modes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r1.anchor: عن سليمان بن صرد، عن أبي بن كعب قال: رحت إلى المسجد، فسمعت رجلا يقرأ فقلت: من أقرأك؟ قال: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says the report is sound in substance from Ubayy and that Sulayman ibn Surad apparently witnessed the event.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r2.anchor: فهذا الحديث محفوظ من حيث الجملة عن أبي بن كعب، والظاهر أن سليمان بن صرد الخزاعي شاهد على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r3.speaker: أبو بكرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r3.claim: Abu Bakra reports that Gabriel and Mika'il granted seven modes, each sufficient, provided a verse of mercy is not joined to one of punishment or vice versa.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p39/r3.anchor: عن أبيه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

TAB-FULL:v1p10/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p10/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p10/r1.claim: The Qur'an's unmatched eloquence and wisdom answer a challenge posed to Arabs renowned for oratory, poetry, rhyme, and soothsaying, making its Arabic expression evidence of revelation.
TAB-FULL:v1p10/r1.anchor: في زمان هم فيه رؤساء صناعة الخطب والبلاغة، وقيل الشعر والفصاحة، والسجع والكهانة

TAB-FULL:v1p10/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p10/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p10/r2.claim: The challengers proved unable to produce comparable speech; an arrogant imitator offered only absurd rhymes, exposing his weakness of mind and tongue.
TAB-FULL:v1p10/r2.anchor: فأتى بما لا يعجز عنه الضعيف الأخرق، والجاهل الأحمق، فقال: والطاحنات طحنا، والعاجنات عجنا

TAB-FULL:v1p3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r1.claim: Creation's signs, including its defects, needs, incapacity, and changing afflictions, point to God's unity and lordship and establish His conclusive proof.
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r1.anchor: فكل موجود إلى وحدانيته داع، وكل محسوس إلى ربوبيته هاد، بما وسمهم به من آثار الصنعة

TAB-FULL:v1p3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r2.claim: God sent messengers with evidences and miracles so people would have no excuse after their coming and could not dismiss them as ordinary humans.
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r2.anchor: وليذكر أولو النهى والحلم؛ فأمدهم بعونه، وأبانهم من سائر خلقه، بما دل به على صدقهم

TAB-FULL:v1p3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r3.claim: God gave prophets different ranks: some received divine speech, while Jesus was strengthened by the Holy Spirit and given power to raise the dead and heal the afflicted and blind.
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r3.anchor: فكرم بعضهم بالتكليم والنجوى، وأيد بعضهم بروح القدس، وخصه بإحياء الموتى، وإبراء أولي العاهة والعمى

TAB-FULL:v1p3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r4.claim: Muhammad was granted the highest prophetic rank, the best portion of divine favor, and the greatest share of followers and companions.
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r4.anchor: وفضل نبينا محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم من الدرجات بالعليا، ومن المراتب بالعظمى

TAB-FULL:v1p3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r5.claim: Muhammad's universal mission was protected from hostile tyrants and devils until he established the religion, clarified truth, and removed idolatry and falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r5.anchor: وابتعثه بالدعوة التامة، والرسالة العامة، وحاطه وحيدا، وعصمه فريدا، من كل جبار عاند

TAB-FULL:v1p3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r6.claim: The Qur'an is Muhammad's enduring miracle, whose light increases across ages, unlike earlier prophets' signs and the traces of their narrower missions, which faded.
TAB-FULL:v1p3/r6.anchor: مؤيدا بدلالة على الأيام باقية، وعلى الدهور والأزمان ثابتة، وعلى ممر الشهور والسنين دائمة

TAB-FULL:v1p5/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p5/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p5/r1.claim: The preserved Qur'an is proof of Muhammad's prophethood and a sign distinguishing truth from falsehood; all jinn and humans together could not produce a surah like it.
TAB-FULL:v1p5/r1.anchor: لو اجتمع جميع من بين أقطارها، من جنها وإنسها، وصغيرها وكبيرها، على أن يأتوا بسورة من مثله

TAB-FULL:v1p5/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p5/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p5/r2.claim: The Qur'an guides those seeking God's favor from darkness to light and serves as the community's refuge, judge, and safeguard in disagreement and crises.
TAB-FULL:v1p5/r2.anchor: فهو موئلهم الذي إليه عند الاختلاف يئلون، ومعقلهم الذي إليه في النوازل يعتقلون

TAB-FULL:v1p5/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p5/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p5/r3.claim: Al-Tabari plans a comprehensive commentary recording communal agreement and disagreement, explaining each school's reasoning, and identifying the soundest position concisely.
TAB-FULL:v1p5/r3.anchor: مخبرون في كل ذلك بما انتهى إلينا من اتفاق الحجة فيما اتفقت عليه الأمة، واختلافها فيما اختلفت فيه

TAB-FULL:v1p11/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p11/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p11/r1.claim: God addresses each people in a language they understand; otherwise revelation would give them no benefit, contrary to God's wisdom, as Ibrahim 14:4 and al-Nahl 16:64 show.
TAB-FULL:v1p11/r1.anchor: ولا يرسل إلى أحد منهم رسولا برسالة إلا بلسان وبيان يفهمه المرسل إليه

TAB-FULL:v1p11/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p11/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p11/r2.claim: Since Muhammad's language was Arabic, the Qur'an is Arabic, as its own declarations affirm.
TAB-FULL:v1p11/r2.anchor: وإذا كان لسان محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عربيا، فبين أن القرآن عربي

TAB-FULL:v1p11/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p11/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p11/r3.claim: Qur'anic meanings and expression accord with Arabic speech, using its rhetorical patterns: brevity or elaboration, omission, repetition, indirect reference, shifts in scope, and reordered elements.
TAB-FULL:v1p11/r3.anchor: موجودا في كلام العرب الإيجاز والاختصار، والاجتزاء بالإخفاء من الإظهار، وبالقلة من الإكثار

TAB-FULL:v1p65/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r1.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that the Qur'an was revealed in five categories: lawful, forbidden, clear, ambiguous, and parables; he instructs believers to observe, believe, and learn from them accordingly.
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، قال: " إن الله أنزل القرآن على خمسة أحرف: حلال، وحرام، ومحكم

TAB-FULL:v1p65/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r2.claim: Al-Tabari treats reports of seven doors and seven letters as compatible expressions for aspects or modes, comparing them with worshipping God on a 'ḥarf' in 22:11, meaning doubtfully or conditionally.
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r2.anchor: فكذلك رواية من روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنه قال: نزل القرآن من سبعة أبواب، ونزل على سبعة أحرف سواء

TAB-FULL:v1p65/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r3.claim: Earlier scriptures came in one language, so another-language rendering is translation; the Qur'an came in seven tongues, and recitation in any of them remains recitation as revealed.
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r3.anchor: وأنزل كتابنا بألسن سبعة، بأي تلك الألسن السبعة تلاه التالي، كان له تاليا على ما أنزله الله

TAB-FULL:v1p65/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r4.claim: The Psalms chiefly remind and admonish, while the Gospel praises and urges forgiveness and turning away; such earlier books contained only one of the Qur'an's seven religious aspects.
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r4.anchor: كزبور داود، الذي إنما هو تذكير ومواعظ، وإنجيل عيسى، الذي هو تمجيد ومحامد وحض على الصفح والإعراض

TAB-FULL:v1p65/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r5.claim: The Qur'an's seven doors to Paradise correspond to obeying commands, avoiding prohibitions, permitting the lawful, forbidding the forbidden, believing its clear text, submitting to its ambiguous text as God's word, and learning from parables.
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r5.anchor: والعمل بما أمر الله جل ذكره في كتابه باب من أبواب الجنة، وترك ما نهى الله عنه فيه باب آخر ثان

TAB-FULL:v1p65/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r6.claim: Each Qur'anic letter or aspect has a divinely imposed boundary no one may cross; its outward side is recitation and its inward side is interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r6.anchor: وأما قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، في القرآن: «إن لكل حرف منه حدا» يعني لكل وجه من أوجهه السبعة حد حده الله جل ثناؤه

TAB-FULL:v1p65/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r7.claim: Each divinely set limit has a corresponding measure of reward or punishment that one encounters in the afterlife; al-Tabari explains the 'rising place' through this encounter.
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r7.anchor: فإنه يعني أن لكل حد من حدود الله التي حدها فيه، من حلال وحرام وسائر شرائعه، مقدارا من ثواب الله وعقابه

TAB-FULL:v1p65/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r8.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r8.claim: Umar says he would ransom all the world's gold and silver to escape the terror of what will confront him after death, illustrating the afterlife encounter.
TAB-FULL:v1p65/r8.anchor: كما قال عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه: «لو أن لي ما في الأرض من صفراء وبيضاء لافتديت به من هول المطلع»

TAB-FULL:v1p69/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r1.claim: The time of the Hour belongs to God alone; the Prophet indicated its signs rather than naming a date, as the Hour passage says.
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r1.anchor: لم يكن عنده علم أوقات شيء منه، بمقادير السنين والأيام، وأن الله جل ثناؤه، إنما كان عرفه مجيئه بأشراطه

TAB-FULL:v1p69/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r2.claim: In a report about the Dajjal, the Prophet says that if he appears during the Prophet's lifetime, the Prophet will contend with him; otherwise God will be the companions' protector.
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r2.anchor: إن يخرج وأنا فيكم، فأنا حجيجه، وإن يخرج بعدي، فالله خليفتي عليكم

TAB-FULL:v1p69/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r3.claim: Arabic speakers can know basic grammar, unique names, referents, and specific descriptions; detailed rulings, qualities, and forms require prophetic explanation, while some knowledge is reserved to God.
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r3.anchor: فإن ذلك لا يجهله أحد منهم، وذلك كسامع منهم لو سمع تاليا يتلو

TAB-FULL:v1p69/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r4.claim: People understand that corruption is harmful and reform beneficial, but may not know which acts God classifies under each term without further explanation.
TAB-FULL:v1p69/r4.anchor: لم يجهل أن معنى الإفساد هو ما ينبغي تركه مما هو مضرة، وأن الإصلاح هو ما ينبغي فعله

TAB-FULL:v1p31/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p31/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v1p31/r1.claim: Ubayy reports that the Prophet approved both recitations he had taught, prayed to remove Ubayy's doubt, and described angels prompting him to increase the recitation from one letter up to seven.
TAB-FULL:v1p31/r1.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: رحت إلى المسجد، فسمعت رجلا، يقرأ، فقلت: من أقرأك

TAB-FULL:v1p31/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p31/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v1p31/r2.claim: In another Ubayy report, the Prophet confirms both readings and describes Gabriel and Michael prompting an increase to seven letters; one transmission is uncertain between six and seven, another states seven.
TAB-FULL:v1p31/r2.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، رضي الله عنه، قال: ما حاك في صدري شيء منذ أسلمت، إلا أني قرأت آية

TAB-FULL:v1p39/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r1.claim: Abu Jahm al-Ansari reports that after two men each claimed to have received a disputed reading from the Prophet, he said the Qur'an came in seven letters and forbade disputation as disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r1.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف، فلا تماروا في القرآن، فإن المراء فيه كفر»

TAB-FULL:v1p39/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r2.claim: A report transmitted by Amr ibn Dinar says the Qur'an was revealed in seven letters, each sufficient and complete.
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r2.anchor: قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف، كلها شاف كاف»

TAB-FULL:v1p39/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet saying he was commanded to recite the Qur'an in seven letters, each adequate and sufficient.
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r3.anchor: عن جده عبد الله بن مسعود، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أمرت أن أقرأ القرآن على سبعة أحرف

TAB-FULL:v1p39/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya reports that five men from different groups recited before the Prophet, who accepted their differing speech forms and said Banu Tamim were the most eloquent.
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r4.anchor: قال: حدثني أبو العالية، قال: «قرأ على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من كل خمس رجل، فاختلفوا في اللغة

TAB-FULL:v1p39/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the seven-letter revelation removes restriction in recitation, but forbids ending a mention of mercy with punishment or punishment with mercy.
TAB-FULL:v1p39/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «إن هذا القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف

BAQILLANI:v1p88/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r1.claim: Hind bint al-Nuʿmān’s reply to al-Mughīra illustrates a preceding rhetorical figure, though its label falls outside this excerpt.
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r1.anchor: قول هند بنت النعمان للمغيرة بن شعبة وقد أحسن إليها برتك يد نالتها خصاصة

BAQILLANI:v1p88/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r2.claim: Muwāzana is counted among the figures of badīʿ; the author illustrates it with balanced poetry and a Qur’anic example.
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r2.anchor: ويعدون من البديع الموازنة وذلك كقول بعضهم أصبر على حر اللقاء ومضض النزال

BAQILLANI:v1p88/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r3.claim: Musāwāt is eloquence in which wording exactly matches the meaning, neither exceeding nor falling short of it; many Qur’anic examples exist.
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r3.anchor: المساواة وهي أن يكون اللفظ مساويا للمعنى لا يزيد عليه ولا ينقص عنه وذلك يعد من البلاغة

BAQILLANI:v1p88/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r4.claim: Ishāra is a brief expression that contains many meanings; the cited Qur’anic formulation exemplifies this compression.
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r4.anchor: الإشارة وهو اشتمال اللفظ القليل على المعاني الكثيرة وقال بعضهم في وصف البلاغة

BAQILLANI:v1p88/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r5.claim: Mubālagha reinforces a statement’s meaning; the cited boastful poems illustrate emphasis, while ghuluw is introduced as another figure with Abū Nuwās as an example.
BAQILLANI:v1p88/r5.anchor: ويعدون من البديع المبالغة والغلو والمبالغة تأكيد معاني القول وذلك كقول الشاعر

BAQILLANI:v1p237/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r1.claim: The first two verses use the poet’s familiar, balanced style but add no invention and have already been surpassed.
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r1.anchor: البيتان الأولان من الجنس الذي يكثر كلامه عليه وهي طريقته التي يجتبيها

BAQILLANI:v1p237/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r2.claim: A poet completing ten verses on a sword should invent fresh material rather than repeat received ideas; al-Mutanabbī supplies a stronger account of its polish and brightness.
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r2.anchor: وسبيله أن يغرب ويبدع كما أبدع المتنبي في قوله

BAQILLANI:v1p237/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r3.claim: The phrase “مصغ إلى حكم الردى” reverses the intended syntax; it should say that death listens to the sword’s judgment, as another poet puts it.
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r3.anchor: مقلوب كان ينبغي أن يقول يصغي الردى إلى حكمه كما قال الآخر

BAQILLANI:v1p237/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r4.claim: “وإذا قضي لم يعدل” is a familiar, repeatedly used poetic formula, especially for this very idea.
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r4.anchor: وقوله وإذا قضي لم يعدل متكرر على ألسنتهم في الشعر خاصة في نفس هذا المعنى

BAQILLANI:v1p237/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r5.claim: The third verse is sound but, like the first two, contains no striking rhetorical invention.
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r5.anchor: والبيت الثالث سليم وهو كالأولين في خلوه عن البديع

BAQILLANI:v1p237/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r6.claim: The claim that every sword strike is fatal makes a verbal effect whose meaning is overstated: a blow may not kill; al-Mutanabbī gives the opposite image, and poets use such claims to boast of spear thrusts and sword cuts.
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r6.anchor: البيت الأول يقصد بمثله صنعه اللفظ وهو في المعنى متفاوت

BAQILLANI:v1p237/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r7.claim: Saying an unbroken sword has “no place to be killed” is strained and nearly impossible language for the intended meaning; a contemporary poet offers a similar image of breaking spear and blade.
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r7.anchor: تعسف لأنه يريد بذلك انه لا ينكسر فالتعبير بما عبر به عن المعنى

BAQILLANI:v1p237/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r8.claim: The image of black and red ants repeats a common poetic meaning; specifying red ants as tiny ants is flat over-detail, and its grammatical inflection is objectionable.
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r8.anchor: والبيت الثاني أيضا هو معنى مكرر على ألسنة الشعراء وأما تصنيعه بسود النمال وحمرها فليس بشيء

BAQILLANI:v1p237/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r9.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r9.claim: The poem’s needless precision recalls a person who itemized the Pleiades’ alignment by tiny measurements; such pedantry is disliked by God and people.
BAQILLANI:v1p237/r9.anchor: كان كذا حين كانت الثريا بحذاء رأسي على سواء أو منحرفا قدر شبر أو نصف شبر

BAQILLANI:v1p156/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r1.claim: The author dismisses Musaylima’s alleged revelation as the lowest and most foolish speech, quoting samples only so readers can recognize its absurdity and the ignorance that misled people.
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r1.anchor: فأما كلام مسيلمة الكذاب وما زعم أنه قرآن فهو أخس من أن نشتغل به وأسخف من أن نفكر فيه

BAQILLANI:v1p156/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r2.speaker: مسيلمة
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r2.claim: Sajāḥ, described as a prophetess, asked Musaylima what had been revealed to him; he recited verses about a pregnant woman and reproduction, after which she affirmed his prophethood.
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r2.anchor: وقالت سجاح بنت الحارث بن عقبان وكانت تتنبأ فاجتمع مسيلمة معها فقالت له ما أوحي إليك

BAQILLANI:v1p156/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r3.claim: The author says he has omitted the rest of Musaylima’s material to avoid burdening the reader with it.
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r3.anchor: ولم ننقل كل ما ذكر من سخفه كراهية التثقيل

BAQILLANI:v1p156/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r4.claim: A report says Abū Bakr asked visitors from Banū Ḥanīfa about these sayings; after hearing samples, he rejected them as speech not from God and wondered how they had been deceived.
BAQILLANI:v1p156/r4.anchor: فقال أبو بكر سبحان الله ويحكم إن هذا الكلام لم يخرج عن إل فأين كان يهذب بكم

BAQILLANI:v1p8/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r1.claim: The Prophet’s other miracles occurred at particular times, circumstances, and audiences; some were mass-transmitted, some witnessed by crowds, and some reported individually.
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r1.anchor: تلك المعجزات قامت في أوقات خاصة وأحوال خاصة وعلى أشخاص خاصة ونقل بعضها نقلا متواترا

BAQILLANI:v1p8/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r2.claim: The Qur’an is a universal, enduring miracle whose proof binds people from its first arrival through every later age; inability in either the first or present generation can establish its force.
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r2.anchor: فأما دلالة القرآن فهي عن معجزة عامة عمت الثقلين وبقيت بقاء العصرين ولزوم الحجة بها

BAQILLANI:v1p8/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r3.claim: An unnamed opponent argues that only the first generation was challenged, so their failure proves the case even if people today could produce the like.
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r3.anchor: حكى عن بعضهم أنه زعم أنه وإن كان قد عجز عنه أهل العصر الأول فليس أهل هذا العصر بعاجزين عنه

BAQILLANI:v1p8/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r4.claim: The author says this restriction of the challenge to the first generation is mistaken and promises to demonstrate the error.
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r4.anchor: ونحن نبين خطأ هذا القول في موضعه إن شاء الله

BAQILLANI:v1p8/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r5.claim: The statement that revelation was sent to guide people entails that it is a proof, and it can be a proof only if it is miraculous.
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r5.anchor: ولا يكون كذلك إلا وهو حجة ولا يكون حجة إن لم يكن معجزة

BAQILLANI:v1p8/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r6.claim: The command to grant a polytheist protection until he hears God’s speech makes hearing the Qur’an a proof against him; such proof must be miraculous.
BAQILLANI:v1p8/r6.anchor: فلولا أن سماعه إياه حجة عليه لم يقف أمره على سماعه ولا يكون حجة إلا وهو معجزة

BAQILLANI:v1p16/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r1.claim: The first premise is that the recited, memorized, written Qur’an is exactly what the Prophet brought and recited for twenty-three years; mass transmission gives necessary certainty of this identity.
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r1.anchor: القرآن الذي هو متلو محفوظ مرسوم في المصاحف هو الذي جاء به النبي وأنه هو الذي تلاه على من في عصره ثلاثا وعشرين سنة

BAQILLANI:v1p16/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r2.claim: Public proclamation, writing to provinces, transmission by followers and non-followers, circulation among adversarial religions, memorization, prayer, legal use, and successive generations preserve the Qur’an’s identity beyond doubt.
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r2.anchor: ثم تناقله خلف عن سلف هم مثلهم في كثرتهم وتوفر دواعيهم على نقله حتى انتهى إلينا على ما وصفناه

BAQILLANI:v1p16/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r3.claim: Once its transmission from God is established, the second premise is that the Prophet challenged people to produce its like and reproached them for failing over many years.
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r3.anchor: وإذا ثبت هذا الأصل وجودا فإنا نقول إنه تحداهم إلى أن يأتوا بمثله وقرعهم على ترك الإتيان به

BAQILLANI:v1p16/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r4.claim: The Qur’an itself states the challenge: doubters should produce a comparable sūra and call their witnesses; failing that, they should fear the Fire.
BAQILLANI:v1p16/r4.anchor: مذكور في القرآن في المواضع الكثيرة كقوله

BAQILLANI:v1p83/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r1.claim: The opening examples of secret and public, benefit and harm, and few and many illustrate another figure counted among badīʿ, though its name is not included here.
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r1.anchor: فسري كإعلاني وتلك سجيتي وظلمة ليلي مثل ضوء نهاريا

BAQILLANI:v1p83/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r2.speaker: الخليل
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl’s definition of tajnīs is that two words resemble one another in the arrangement of their letters and meaning.

BAQILLANI:v1p83/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r3.claim: Others define tajnīs by shared derivation, illustrating it with Qur’anic pairs such as “الدين القيم,” “مع سليمان,” “أسفى على يوسف,” and “ينهون عنه وينأون عنه.”
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r3.anchor: ومنهم من زعم أن المجانسة أن تشترك اللفظتان على جهة الاشتقاق

BAQILLANI:v1p83/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r4.claim: Further tajnīs examples include the Prophet’s wordplay on tribal names, “الظلم ظلمات,” “ذو الوجهين وجيها,” and sayings and poems by Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUmar, Qays ibn ʿĀṣim, and other poets.
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r4.anchor: وكقول النبي أسلم سالمها الله وغفار غفر الله لها وعصية عصت الله ورسوله

BAQILLANI:v1p83/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r5.claim: The author continues the figure’s examples with wordplay in letters and verse, including lines transmitted through al-Akhfash, al-Mubarrad, and al-Tawzī.
BAQILLANI:v1p83/r5.anchor: أنشدنا الأخفش عن المبرد عن التوزي

BURHAN:v4p426/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p426/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p426/r3.claim: مع means accompaniment between two matters sharing an action or ruling; its complete sense is shared participation in the matter, not necessarily simultaneity. In 12:36 it marks the youths entering prison alongside Joseph.
BURHAN:v4p426/r3.anchor: وكمال معنى المعية الاجتماع في الأمر الذي به الاشتراك دون زمانه فالأول يكثر

BURHAN:v2p277/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p277/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p277/r8.claim: The dreamer calls it bread although birds eat grain, because grain is what the bread will become; the author says scholars usually cite only the wine example.
BURHAN:v2p277/r8.anchor: أي لأن الذي تأكل الطير منه إنما هو البر لا الخبز

BURHAN:v2p277/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p277/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p277/r9.claim: “I am pressing wine” means grapes, named for the wine they will become.
BURHAN:v2p277/r9.anchor: أي عنبا فعبر عنه لأنه آيل إلى الخمرية

BURHAN:v2p277/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p277/r10.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p277/r10.claim: One view denies metaphor because خمر is itself a lexical name for grapes in the language of Azd Oman; al-Farisi reports this from Ibn Durayd.
BURHAN:v2p277/r10.anchor: نقله الفارسي في التذكرة عن غريب القرآن لابن دريد

BURHAN:v2p277/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p277/r11.speaker: ابن جني
BURHAN:v2p277/r11.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the wording as naming the cause (grapes) by its effect (wine).
BURHAN:v2p277/r11.anchor: وقيل اكتفى بالمسبب الذي هو الخمر عن السبب الذي هو العنب قاله ابن جني في الخصائص

BURHAN:v2p277/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p277/r12.speaker: ابن عزيز
BURHAN:v2p277/r12.claim: Ibn Aziz locates the figurative usage in the verb أعصر, which means “extract,” rather than in the noun خمر.
BURHAN:v2p277/r12.anchor: واليه ذهب ابن عزيز في غريبه

ITQAN:v2p516#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p516#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p516#3/r1.claim: Maʿa is a noun, as its genitive construction with min shows, and can mean ʿinda; its basic sense involves sharing place or time.
ITQAN:v2p516#3/r1.anchor: اسم بدليل جرها بمن في قراءة بعضهم ﴿ هذا ذكر من معي ﴾ وهي بمعنى عند وأصلها لمكان الاجتماع أو وقته نحو

ITQAN:v2p516#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p516#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p516#3/r2.claim: Maʿa may express simple association or participation without reference to a shared place or time, as in being with the truthful or worshippers.
ITQAN:v2p516#3/r2.anchor: وقد يراد به مجرد الاجتماع والاشتراك من غير ملاحظة المكان والزمان نحو ﴿ وكونوا مع الصادقين ﴾ ﴿ واركعوا مع الراكعين ﴾

ITQAN:v2p516#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p516#3/r4.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p516#3/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib says the word following maʿa as its complement is the intended focus in these constructions.
ITQAN:v2p516#3/r4.anchor: قال الراغب والمضاف إليه لفظ مع هو المقصود كالآيات المذكورة

ITQAN:v4p387/r29.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p387/r29.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p387/r29.claim: One identification of the two prison youths gives the names Mijlath and his sons, including the cupbearer.
ITQAN:v4p387/r29.anchor: ﴿ ودخل معه السجن فتيان ﴾ هو مجلث وبنوه وهو الساقي

ITQAN:v4p387/r30.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p387/r30.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p387/r30.claim: An alternative identification names the youths Rāshān and Marṭash.

ITQAN:v4p387/r31.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p387/r31.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p387/r31.claim: Another alternative names the youths Sharham and Sarham.

ITQAN:v2p378/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p378/r11.speaker: الضحاك
ITQAN:v2p378/r11.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains أعصر خمرا as pressing grapes; Omanis call grapes khamr.
ITQAN:v2p378/r11.anchor: وأخرج عن الضحاك في قوله تعالى ﴿ أعصر خمرا ﴾ قال عنبا بلغة أهل عمان يسمون العنب خمرا

ITQAN:v3p101/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p101/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p101/r3.claim: A thing may be named by what it will become: grapes are called wine, future disbelievers sinners, a betrothed man a husband, and a child by later traits.
ITQAN:v3p101/r3.anchor: تسميته باسم ما يؤول إليه نحو ﴿ إني أراني أعصر خمرا ﴾ أي عنبا يؤول إلى الخمرية

ITQAN:v4p335/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p335/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p335/r6.claim: The Qur'an mentions essential crafts and tools: sewing, smithing, building, shipbuilding, spinning, weaving, farming, hunting, diving, jewelry, glass and pottery work, navigation, writing, breadmaking, cooking, washing, laundering, and butchery.
ITQAN:v4p335/r6.anchor: وفيه أصول الصنائع وأسماء الآلات التي تدعو الضرورة إليها كالخياطة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r1.claim: With a cognate accusative, the statement attributes the action to its agent, not the object as an action; فعل زيد الضرب makes the beating Zayd's act.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r1.anchor: فيما منصوبة مفعول وليس مفعولا به يتعلق بنفس المفعول فإذا قلت فعل زيد الضرب كنت أثبت الضرب فعلا لزيد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r2.claim: With a direct object, the derived action is asserted as occurring to it: أحيا الله زيدا asserts life as God's act in Zayd, while asserting Zayd's creation requires خلق.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r2.anchor: نحو ضربت زيدا أنك أثبت زيدا مضروبا فإن ذلك يرجع إلى انك تثبت الضرب واقعا به منك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r3.claim: To judge a sentence literal or metaphorical, ask whether the assertion is assigned to its proper locus and whether the asserted meaning itself is literal or transferred.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p319/r3.anchor: تنظر إليها من جهتين إحداهما أن تنظر إلى ما وقع بها من الإثبات أهو في حقه وموضعه أم قد زال عن الموضع

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r1.claim: A sentence is clearly metaphorical when its grammatical subject cannot cause the event, as in saying love brought someone to you or words brought ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ from Syria.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r1.anchor: ما لا يدعى أحد من المحقين والمبطلين أنه مما يصح أن يكون له تأثير في وجود المعنى الذي أثبت له وذلك نحو قول الرجل محبتك جاءت بي إليك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r2.claim: When a speaker's monotheist belief is known, attributing aging or destruction to days and nights is metaphorical; the intended true agent is the capable Creator.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r2.anchor: أنه يكون قد علم من اعتقاد المتكلم أنه لا يثبت الفعل إلا للقادر وأنه ممن لا يعتقد الاعتقادات الفاسدة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r3.claim: Abū al-Najm first assigns aging to passing nights, then clarifies that God ordered the sun to rise and set, revealing the figurative attribution.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p337/r3.anchor: ثم فسر وكشف عن وجه التأول وأفاد أنه بنى أول كلامه على التخيل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r1.claim: Jurjani divides metaphorical transfer into transfers with no benefit and transfers with benefit, then turns first to the limited, non-beneficial kind.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r1.anchor: تنقسم أولا قسمين أحدهما أن لا يكون لنقله فائدة والثاني أن يكون له فائدة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r2.claim: Animal-specific names for the same body part reflect fine distinctions in Arabic usage; using one for another species is a transfer from its original scope.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r2.anchor: وضعهم للعضو الواحد أسامي كثيرة بحسب اختلاف أجناس الحيوان

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r3.speaker: العجاج
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r3.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj calls a bright nose مرسن, borrowing a term originally used for the part on which an animal's bridle rests.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r3.anchor: كقول العجاج وفاحما ومر سنا مسرجا يعنى أنفا برق كالسراج والمرسن في الأصل للحيوان

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r4.claim: An unnamed poet describing camels applies الجحفل, a term from the horse's mouth vocabulary, to one of the camels.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r4.anchor: تسمع للماء كصوت المسحل بين وريدها وبين الجحفل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r5.claim: A poet uses الحفان for young camels, though the word is originally assigned to young ostriches.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r5.anchor: وقال آخر والحشو من حفانها كالحنظل فأجرى الحفان على صغار الإبل وهو موضوع لصغار النعام

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses شفة for a horse, although that body-part name is assigned to humans.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r6.anchor: فاستعمل الشفة في الفرس وهي موضوعة للإنسان

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r7.claim: These transfers add no semantic content: شفتيه and جحفلتيه would both identify the same known body part.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r7.anchor: لا فرق من جهة المعنى بين قوله من شفتيه وقوله من جحفلتيه لو قاله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r8.claim: A species-specific name identifies both the organ and its animal; metaphorical transfer turns that restriction into shared usage and can make the referent ambiguous.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r8.anchor: زالت عنها هذه الدلالة بانقلاب اختصاصها إلى الاشتراك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r9.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r9.claim: In a context mentioning both a person and a horse, transferred شفة can prompt doubt that the horse is intended; without the transfer, that ambiguity would not arise.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p22#2/r9.anchor: دخل على السامع بعض الشبهة لتجويزه أن تكون استعرت الاسم للفرس ولو فرضنا أن تعدم هذه الاستعارة من أصلها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r2.claim: He attributes the persistence of false objections to neglect of reflection, weak intention, and low ambition, which leave people receptive to baseless claims.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r2.anchor: وإهمال التدبر وضعف النية وقصر الهمة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r3.claim: The ṣarfa theory also fails: if God merely diverted the Arabs from composing a rival, their wonder would concern their imposed incapacity rather than the Qur’an’s intrinsic excellence.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r4.claim: He compares ṣarfa to a prophet whose ordinary gesture is made impossible for everyone else: observers would marvel at their own inability, not at the gesture as a miracle.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p291/r4.anchor: أرأيت لو أن نبيا قال لقومه : ' إن آيتي أن أضع يدي على رأسي هذه الساعة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r1.claim: An image and its explanatory paraphrase may convey related content but do not have equal rhetorical force; treating them as interchangeable would erase the merits of metaphor and idiom.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r1.anchor: ولا مزية لقوله : ألقيت حبله على غاربه . على قولك في تفسيره : خليته وما يريد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r2.claim: Calling a brave man أسد claims that he is a lion and is stronger than the prose paraphrase that he is as brave as one.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r2.anchor: ولم تكن قد زدت في المعنى بأن ادعيت له أنه أسد بالحقيقة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r6.claim: Al-Mutanabbī’s line وتأبى الطباع على الناقل is not equivalent to the plain statement that human nature cannot be changed.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r6.anchor: من أن لا يكون فرق بين قول المتنبي : ( وتأبى الطباع على الناقل ) وبين قولهم : إنك لا تقدر أن تغير طباع الإنسان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r7.claim: Abū Nuwās’s line about God gathering the world in one is stronger in form than the prose paraphrase about gathering all human virtues in one person.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r7.anchor: ويجعلوا حال المعنى في قول أبي نواس : ( وليس لله بمستنكر أن يجمع العالم في واحد )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r9.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r9.claim: Lexical explanation works by replacing a rare word with a familiar synonym, as with شرجب meaning الطويل, القط meaning الكتاب, and الدسر meaning المسامير; that does not make rhetorical paraphrase equivalent to the original.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r9.anchor: إنه + الطويل + وفي القط إنه الكتاب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r1.claim: The Qur’an’s exact recitation and preservation keep its proof standing through every age and make it available for later generations to learn and transmit.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r1.anchor: إلا لتكون الحجة به قائمة على وجه الدهر تعرف في كل زمان ، ويتوصل إليها في كل أوان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r2.claim: Preventing access to the source from which proof is drawn is equivalent to preventing access to the proof itself, just as withholding a remedy resembles withholding knowledge that it heals.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r2.anchor: فسواء من منعك الشيء الذي ينتزع منه الشاهد والدليل ، ومن منعك السبيل إلى انتزاع تلك الدلالة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r3.speaker: قائل منهم
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r3.claim: An opponent proposes a different proof of inimitability: the Arabs’ inability to match the Qur’an despite repeated challenges, a historical fact that can also convince non-Arabs.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r3.anchor: فإن قال منهم قائل : إنك قد أغفلت فيما رتبت ، فإن لنا طريقا إلى إعجاز القرآن غير ما قلت

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r4.claim: The lasting miracle means that the Qur’an’s inimitable quality remains present and that anyone seeking knowledge can still find and understand its proof.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r4.anchor: لا معنى لبقاء المعجزة بالقرآن إلا أن الوصف الذي له كان معجزا قائم فيه أبدا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r5.claim: He rebukes preferring imitation and ignorance to learning God’s proof, since that choice leaves its authority less able to prevail over idolatry and unbelief.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p26/r5.anchor: وكان التقليد فيها أحب إليك ، والتعويل على علم غيرك آثر لديك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r1.claim: The Qur’an’s inimitability cannot rest merely on smooth delivery or freedom from difficult consonant clusters; those traits do not define excellence or explain differences in eloquence.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r1.anchor: لأنه ليس بذلك كان الكلام كلاما ، ولا هو بالذي يتناهى أمره إن عد في الفضيلة إلى أن يكون الأصل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r2.claim: Accounts of the challenge describe the Arabs as poets, orators, and masters of eloquence, expression, and judgment, not as specialists in avoiding heavy sound combinations.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r2.anchor: إن النبي تحداهم وفيهم الشعراء والخطباء والذين يدلّون بفصاحة اللسان ، والبراعة ، والبيان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r3.claim: The received comparison of prophetic miracles is that each answered the dominant expertise of its audience: Moses overcame magic, Jesus displayed healing and revival, and Muhammad’s sign was eloquence and varied composition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r3.anchor: ولما انتهوا إلى ذكر نبينا محمد وذكر ما كان الغالب على زمانه لم يذكروا إلا البلاغة والبيان والتصرف في ضروب النظم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r4.claim: He repeats this argument because people persistently defend the view that the Qur’an’s excellence lies only in wording.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p342/r4.anchor: ليس تهالك الناس في حديث اللفظ ، والمحاماة على الإعتقاد الذي اعتقدوه ، فيه ، وضن أنفسهم به إلى حد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r1.claim: When judging a genre, assess the qualities belonging to that genre; wisdom or unusual content may be valuable, but it does not establish a poem’s merit as poetry.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r1.anchor: من حكم من قضى في جنس من الأجناس بفضل أو نقص أن لا يعتبر في قضيته تلك إلا الأوصاف التي تخص ذلك الجنس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r2.claim: Speech is like a crafted object and meaning is its material, as silver or gold is shaped into a ring; judging composition by meaning alone confuses the craft with its substrate.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r2.anchor: فكما أن محالا إذا أنت أردت النظر في صوغ الخاتم وفي جودة العمل ورداءته أن ينظر إلى الفضة الحاملة تلك الصورة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r3.claim: A ring is not better workmanship merely because its silver is better, just as a poem is not better as poetry merely because its meaning is weightier.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r3.anchor: كذلك ينبغي إذا فضلنا بيتا على بيت من أجل معناه أن لا يكون ذلك تفضيلا له من حيث هو شعر وكلام ، وهذا قاطع فاعرفه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r4.claim: Al-Jurjānī says the treatises on eloquence and earlier critics reject judging rhetoric by meaning alone, and that al-Jāḥiẓ argues especially forcefully against it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r4.anchor: وإذا نظرت في كتب الجاحظ وجدته يبلغ في ذلك كل مبلغ ، ويتشدد غاية التشدد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r5.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ treats knowledge of a poem’s meaning as shared by specialists and ordinary people, while evaluation of its quality requires a discerning eye.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r5.anchor: وقد انتهى في ذلك إلى أن جعل العلم بالمعنى مشتركا ، وسوى فيه بين الخاصة والعامة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو الشيباني
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r6.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ reports that Abū ʿAmr admired two verses so much that, on a Friday in the main mosque, he had someone bring paper and ink to write them down.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r6.anchor: وأنا سمعت أبا عمرو الشيباني وقد بلغ من استجادته لهذين البيتين ، ونحن في المسجد الجامع يوم الجمعة أن كلف رجلا حتى أحضره قرطاسا ودواة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r7.speaker: الجاحظ
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r7.claim: Al-Jāḥiẓ jokes that the author of the two admired verses never writes poetry and that his son will not either, unless he claims knowledge of the unseen.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p196/r7.anchor: قال الجاحظ : وأنا أزعم أن صاحب هذين البيتين لا يقول شعرا أبدا ، ولولا أن أدخل في الحكومة بعض الغيب

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r4.speaker: علي بن الحسين
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r4.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn reports Iqra as the first Meccan revelation; he gives al-Mu’minun or al-Ankabut as the last Meccan surah, al-Mutaffifin first in Medina, Bara’a last there, and al-Najm as the first surah taught in Mecca.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p12/r4.anchor: علي بن الحسين يقول: أول سورة نزلت

DAMGHANI:v1p350/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p350/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p350/r2.claim: The two fityān are the young men who accompanied Joseph when he entered prison.
DAMGHANI:v1p350/r2.anchor: الرابع الفتين الغلامان اللذان صاحبا يوسف عند دخوله السجن

DAMGHANI:v1p20/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p20/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p20/r1.claim: The man who says he sees himself pressing wine is the king’s cupbearer.

DAMGHANI:v1p146/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r3.claim: Ḥaml can mean literal carrying, as with carrying thornwood on one’s back or bread over one’s head.
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r3.anchor: السابع : الحمل بعينه قوله تعالى في سورة المسد

DAMGHANI:v1p362/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r14.claim: Fawq can mean physically over someone or something, including above the head.
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r14.anchor: السادس فوق يعني فوق رؤوسهم قوله تعالى في سورة الاعراف

DAMGHANI:v1p362/r17.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r17.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r17.claim: The entry’s list gives victory as a further sense of fawq, but this excerpt supplies no example for it.
DAMGHANI:v1p362/r17.anchor: ف وق على تسعة اوجه اكبر اكثر افضل ارفع منزلة اعلى فوق الرؤوس قبل المشرق السلطان الظفر

DAMGHANI:v1p59/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p59/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p59/r1.claim: Taʾwīl can mean interpreting a dream; Joseph’s request for its interpretation is grouped with his statement about interpreting reports.

DAMGHANI:v1p347/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p347/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p347/r15.claim: Fityān can mean the two young men who accompanied Joseph into prison.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p218/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p218/r1.claim: Taʾwīl can mean interpreting a dream, as in Joseph's request and the cupbearer's later offer to explain it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p218/r1.anchor: والرابع : تعبير الرؤيا ، ومنه قوله تعالى في يوسف : ﴿ وكذلك يجتبيك ربك ويعلمك من تأويل الأحاديث ﴾ ، وفيها : ^ ( نبئنا بتأويله )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p218/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p218/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p218/r2.claim: Taʾwīl can also mean realization or fulfillment, as in Joseph's statement that the dream had come true.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p218/r2.anchor: والخامس : التحقيق ، ومنه قوله تعالى في يوسف : ^ ( هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r1.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r1.claim: Abu Zakariya says ʿalā functions as a noun, a verb, or a preposition.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r1.anchor: قال أبو زكريا : ' على ' تستعمل اسما وفعلا وحرفا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r2.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r2.claim: When ʿAlā is a person's name it is a noun and accepts case markers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r2.anchor: فإذا كانت عبارة عن شخص فهي اسم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r3.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r3.claim: When it means “above,” ʿalā is also a noun; two poetic lines use it in this sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r3.anchor: وإذا كانت بمعنى فوق فهي اسم أيضا . تقول : جئت من عليه ، كما يقال : جئت من فوقه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r4.claim: Two poets use ʿalā as a noun meaning above: “from above it” and “from on high.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r4.anchor: غدت من عليه بعدما تم ظمؤها وقال الآخر : - فهي تنوش الحوض نوشا من علا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r5.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r5.claim: When derived from a verbal root and denoting a specific time, ʿalā is a verb; otherwise it is a preposition governing the next word.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r5.anchor: وإذا كانت مشتقة من مصدر ودلت على زمان مخصوص فهي فعل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r6.claim: In the other uses, ʿalā is a preposition governing the following word.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r6.anchor: وما عدا هذين الموضعين فهي حرف يجر ما بعدها .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r7.claim: One Qur'anic use of ʿalā means “above,” as in God's establishment over the Throne.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r7.anchor: أحدها : بمعنى فوق . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في طه ] : ﴿ الرحمن على العرش استوى ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r8.claim: A second use means a condition or stipulation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r8.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى الشرط . ومنه قوله تعالى في القصص : ﴿ على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r9.claim: A third use means a guarantee or undertaking.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r9.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى الضمان والالتزام . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في النحل ] : ﴿ وعلى الله قصد السبيل ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r10.claim: A fourth use means “from”; Ibn Qutayba gives another example in which the two heirs are from among those entitled.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r10.anchor: والرابع : بمعنى ' من ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في المطففين : ﴿ الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون ﴾ . قال ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r11.speaker: المبرد
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r11.claim: A fifth use means “in,” as al-Mubarrad explains in the phrase about what devils recited in Solomon's kingdom.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p441/r11.anchor: والخامس : بمعنى ' في ' ومنه قوله تعالى [ في البقرة ] : ( واتبعوا ما تتلوا الشياطين على ملك سليمان ) ^ ، قاله المبرد
